subject: StratusHealth: SLA & throughput follow-up — hosted vs dedicated recommendation
messages:
From: Eric Gomez <eric@stratushealth.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T16:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today — performance needs

Thanks for the time today, Aditya. Quick recap of the key constraints from our side: we run an automated clinical note summarization pipeline that needs to sit behind our EHR. Target production profile: ~150 sustained QPS for short summaries (avg 120 tokens) with spikes up to 500 QPS for ~1–3 minutes during batch ingestion windows. Our internal SLA target is P95 <= 50ms for inference; P99 ideally < 200ms.

Data residency: must remain in our VPC (we host in us-east-1) and we need audit logs/auditing access for SOC 2.

Questions:
- Can Redwood hit P95 <= 50ms at 150 QPS on Hosted? If not, what Dedicated footprint do you recommend?
- What does fallback look like if dedicated capacity degrades?
- Any quick pilot approach you suggest (timeboxed, measurable)?

Appreciate a short recommendation and a proposed next step. I can pull in procurement if we have a rough cost cadence.

—Eric
Eric Gomez
Head of Integrations, StratusHealth

From: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T19:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today — performance needs

Eric — thanks, great notes. Below is a concise recommendation and an actionable pilot plan based on the numbers you shared.

Short answer upfront: Dedicated capacity is the most reliable way to meet a sustained P95 <= 50ms at 150 QPS with the headroom for 500 QPS spikes. Hosted can sometimes meet it for short bursts if we use premium routing and aggressive caching, but it is not the guaranteed path for your SLA and VPC requirement.

Why Dedicated for your profile (summary):
- Predictable per-GPU throughput: continuous batching + pinned kernels minimize jitter at high sustained QPS.
- Isolation: Dedicated gives you capacity isolation and predictable cold-start characteristics important for tight P95s.
- VPC/private option: Redwood Private + Dedicated node placement allows integration into your VPC and audit controls.

Trade-offs vs Hosted:
- Hosted: faster to start (no infra setup), lower ops from your side, but weaker isolation and routing variability during cross-tenant spikes. Might meet P95 at 150 QPS in best-case but not SLA-backed.
- Dedicated: higher committed cost but consistent latency and a clear path to meet your P95 target.

Pilot proposal (2 weeks, success metrics):
1) Week 0 (prep): small Dedicated pool provisioned in your us-east-1 VPC with a single model variant (quantized where acceptable). We provide a test harness and a short qps-profile CSV (attach).
2) Week 1: Load test at ramped QPS: 50 -> 150 sustained, then 500 burst tests. Measure P50/P95/P99, token cost, and GPU utilization.
3) Week 2: Production-like integration with a subset of traffic behind feature flag, monitoring for client-perceived latency and logging.

Success criteria: P95 <= 50ms for sustained 150 QPS; 500 QPS bursts handled with graceful degradation (fallback to a compatible fallback model with controlled latency and throughput).

Cost signal: estimate of dedicated footprint: 4x A100-equivalent nodes (we'll refine after initial profiling) — roughs will be shared in the SOW.

Next steps I propose:
- If you agree, I’ll draft an SOW and pilot onboarding checklist and loop Anna in procurement.
- We’ll attach the SLA draft and a qps sample (see attachments).

I’ll wait for confirmation to stand up pilot capacity.

Thanks — Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Adding notes from an ops/implementation perspective so we can be ready if Eric says yes.

Implementation checklist (ops):
- VPC peering / Private link: engineering to provision cross-account endpoint in us-east-1; security will need subnet CIDR ranges and a short maintenance window.
- Model variant & quantization: recommend starting with FP16 for benchmark runs; if results are good we can try 4-bit quant to reduce nodes.
- Autoscale policy: configure reserved dedicated pool + burst buffer for short windows; set automatic fallback routing to hosted-compatible variant in case of node failure.
- Monitoring: wire up per-route latency dashboards; add token-level cost telemetry.

Risks to call out:
- If your summaries average >200 tokens rather than 120, GPU footprint increases ~20–30% which affects node count. Tell them to share a token distribution sample (we can run a quick profiler).
- Network egress limits from the VPC could add 5–15ms; we should test within their VPC to capture this.

I’ll build the pilot runbook and pilot alerting playbook (approx 3–4 hours each) and drop into the shared drive link. If procurement needs a line-item estimate we can provide a 30-day reserved price for the pilot nodes.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
